correctness.rationale: A proper coloring of a complete multipartite graph uses disjoint palettes on distinct parts. The odd-neighborhood condition is therefore equivalent to having at least two parts with an odd-sized color class. This equivalence yields the three parity cases and the counting formulas. Exhaustive replay verifies minimality and counts on 32 small instances.

originality.rationale: Targeted searches of current scholarly sources and the published-finding corpus found the foundational odd-coloring papers and later product/sparse/complexity work but no equivalent or stronger complete-multipartite parity formula or optimal-coloring enumeration. This remains a best-of-knowledge assessment, not a proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The result gives an exact closed form and complete optimal-coloring enumeration for an infinite classical family, including a sharp parity classification for every complete bipartite graph, with a reusable active-part reduction.
